items.title: Classify reflected input before testing browser execution
items.objective: Determine whether reflected input can cross its exact HTML, attribute, JavaScript, CSS, or URL parser boundary.
prerequisites: A confirmed attacker-influenceable source and browser rendering path
A clean supported browser and designated test account/content
steps: Place a unique inert marker through the reflected source and record every occurrence
For HTML text, test only whether contextual encoding prevents creation of a new element boundary
For quoted or unquoted attributes, test whether the value can escape its quote/delimiter and create an event or active attribute
For JavaScript strings, template literals, and JSON-in-script, test whether the value can escape its exact string/expression grammar
For URL attributes, test parsing and allowlisted schemes without loading external active content
Trace the final parsed DOM and reproduce only a harmless local marker in a clean browser

examples.note: Use a unique harmless DOM-visible marker only. Source: a query, path, body, or header value reflected in an HTML response. Sink: the exact browser parser context at the final reflection.

items.manipulate: a query, path, body, or header value reflected in an HTML response, using only syntax needed for the confirmed parser context
items.secure_behavior: Untrusted values remain data through contextual output encoding, safe DOM APIs, or a maintained allowlist sanitizer at the final sink.
items.vulnerable_behavior: a harmless unique marker becomes executable only after context-appropriate boundary escape
items.validation: Trace source to final sink, reproduce in a clean browser under the application origin, and prove a realistic delivery/victim context.
false_positives: literal marker text is contextually encoded
a proxy or browser extension injects the apparent reflection
items.impact: Confirmed XSS can perform victim-authorized actions, alter trusted content, read origin-accessible data, or pivot across application workflows subject to victim privilege and browser defenses.
evidence: Source request or state with secrets redacted
Raw response, parsed DOM, and source-to-sink trace
Harmless execution marker in a clean browser
Victim interaction, authentication, CSP, and origin context
